overview.text:
**Changed**
- New `_dokuwiki_row` in `tabulate/__init__.py` escapes `|`/`^` as `%%|%%`/`%%^%%` and rewrites each cell's padding by alignment. [E9, H4]
- Right/decimal cells get `"  "+value.rstrip()+" "`, center `"  "+value+"  "`, left `" "+value.lstrip()+"  "`, default `" "+strip+" "`. [H4]
- New `_table_formats["dokuwiki"]` entry: all `line*` set to `None`, `headerrow` uses `^`, `datarow` uses `|`, `padding=0`. [H5]
- Format listings updated in the `tabulate` docstring (plus a doctest), the `cli.py` help, the README list and CLI help, and a new README section. [H1, H2, H3, H6, H7, H8]

**Why**
- User asked for a `dokuwiki` format: `^` header and `|` data separators, no rules, padding-based alignment, safe literal separators, registration and tests. [E1]
- The agent said cells arrive already padded, so it re-trims padding so short cells don't read as centered. [E7]
- The agent maps decimal to right alignment, per the code comment and README. [H2, H4]
- It consulted DokuWiki `syntax.txt` and `handler.php` for the conventions. [E6, E8]

**Tests**
- `test_dokuwiki`, `test_dokuwiki_headerless`: `_test_table` with and without headers; assert exact `^`/`|` output. [H10]
- `test_dokuwiki_alignment`: parametrized over left/right/center/decimal/None on `[["x"],["long"]]`. [H10]
- `test_dokuwiki_header_alignment` uses `headersglobalalign="center"`. Its first run failed; the expected string was then edited to match actual output. [E11, E12, H10]
- Other tests: `_escape_separators` (`a|b`, `c^d`, `|^`), `_empty_cells` (None/""), `_empty_table`, `_registered` (`"dokuwiki" in tabulate_formats`). [H10]
- `pytest -k dokuwiki`: 1 failed, then 12 passed. [E11, E19]
- Full `test_output.py` plus README/`__init__` doctests: 209 passed, 21 skipped, per agent; raw output truncated. [E12, E13]

**Risks**
- Escaping happens after width calculation, so escaped cells overflow and columns misalign in raw text. Accepted in tests (e.g. `| %%|%%%%^%%    |`). [H4, H10]
- Header-alignment expectation was fitted to observed output, not derived from the DokuWiki spec. [E11, H10]
- Ruff with the repo config failed both times (190 errors in E16; still exit 1 in E17). The "lint passed" claim rests on a hand-picked `--select` set. [E16, E17, E19, E20]
- `ruff format --check` initially wanted to reformat the test file; it was patched, then passed. [E17, E18, E19]
- Not verified: rendering in a real DokuWiki, multiline cells, the CLI path. Not shown.
- The agent read outside the repo (`~/.codex/memories`, `agent-readback` AGENTS.md); these were read-only. [E3, E4]

   - It escapes `|`→`%%|%%` and `^`→`%%^%%`. [H4]
   - right/decimal → `"  "+v.rstrip()+" "`; center → two spaces each side; left → `" "+v.lstrip()+"  "`; default strips the value. [H4]
6. Edit: registered `"dokuwiki"` in `_table_formats` with all `line*` set to `None`, `headerrow=partial(..., "^")`, `datarow=partial(..., "|")`, `padding=0`. [E9, H5]

   - The failure was `test_dokuwiki_header_alignment`. [E11]

    - The default run found 190 errors, including `RUF022` on `__all__` and `RUF100` on unchanged lines. [E16]
    - `ruff format --check` wanted to reflow the `tabulate(...)` call in `test_dokuwiki_escape_separators`. [E17]

    - Rendering in real DokuWiki was not checked, including adjacent `%%|%%%%^%%` escapes and header/data width mismatch. [E10, H10]
    - Right alignment emits only one trailing space, not two. [H4]

mechanism.text:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["tabulate(rows, headers, tablefmt='dokuwiki')"] --> B["_table_formats['dokuwiki'] TableFormat"]
  B -->|"all line* = None"| C["no rule lines emitted"]
  B -->|"header cells, already width-padded"| D["partial(_dokuwiki_row, '^')"]
  B -->|"data cells, already width-padded"| E["partial(_dokuwiki_row, '|')"]
  D --> F["_dokuwiki_row(separator, cell_values, colwidths, colaligns)"]
  E --> F
  F -->|"each value"| G["escape: '|' -> '%%|%%', '^' -> '%%^%%'"]
  G --> H{"align"}
  H -->|"right / decimal"| I["'  ' + value.rstrip() + ' '"]
  H -->|"center"| J["'  ' + value + '  '"]
  H -->|"left"| K["' ' + value.lstrip() + '  '"]
  H -->|"other / None"| L["' ' + value.strip() + ' '"]
  I --> M["separator + separator.join(cells) + separator"]
  J --> M
  K --> M
  L --> M
```

- `"dokuwiki"` is registered in `_table_formats`. `lineabove`, `linebelowheader`, `linebetweenrows` and `linebelow` are all `None`, so no rule lines are emitted. It sets `padding=0` [H5].
- `headerrow` binds `_dokuwiki_row` with `"^"` and `datarow` binds it with `"|"`. Headers therefore render as `^ … ^` and data as `| … |` [H5, H4].
- tabulate has already padded each cell to column width before `_dokuwiki_row` runs. The row function strips the padding on the aligned side and re-adds DokuWiki spacing [E7, H4].
- Escaping runs after width computation and wraps separators in `%%…%%`. Escaped rows are visually misaligned, e.g. `| %%|%%%%^%%    |`, and `test_dokuwiki_escape_separators` pins that output [H4, H10].
- `right`/`decimal` produce `"  "+rstrip+" "`. Decimal digits lose column alignment, e.g. `|   451 |` vs `|    41.9999 |` in `test_dokuwiki`. This branch is also covered by the `right` and `decimal` cases of `test_dokuwiki_alignment` [H4, H10].
- The `left` branch is hit by string columns in `test_dokuwiki` and by the `left` case. The `None` case reaches the fallback `strip()` branch (`| x |`) [H10].
- `center` keeps tabulate's centered padding and adds two spaces on each side. In E11, `test_dokuwiki_header_alignment` expected `^  name   ^` but got `^   name   ^` [E11].
- The final test expects the observed `^   name   ^` output. Whether E12 also changed `_dokuwiki_row` is not shown [E12, H10].
- Other edge-case tests: `test_dokuwiki_empty_cells` checks that separators stay for `None`/`""` cells. `test_dokuwiki_empty_table` checks `""` and a header-only row. `test_dokuwiki_registered` checks membership in `tabulate_formats` [H10].
- Verification: `pytest -k dokuwiki` passed 12/12, and broader tests plus doctests reported 209 passed, 21 skipped [E12, E13, E19].
- Lint only passed with a hand-picked `--select` list; default ruff config reported 190 errors [E16, E19].
- Rendering in an actual DokuWiki instance was not verified [E19].
